# Redwood Inference — Marketplace FAQ

This FAQ answers common questions about purchasing Redwood Inference through AWS Marketplace or Google Cloud Marketplace (GCP Marketplace), including procurement, subscription activation, entitlements, billing, credits/trials, security, and support.

If you don’t see your question here, contact us at support@redwoodinference.com or your Redwood account team.

---

## 1) Procurement & purchasing

### Q: What can I buy via marketplace?
You can purchase Redwood Inference through marketplace for:
- Hosted API (usage-based inference)
- Dedicated capacity (reserved / committed capacity offerings)
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem offerings, where available through marketplace procurement paths)
- Add-ons (e.g., compliance/security add-ons, premium support, or observability retention), depending on the marketplace listing and your negotiated offer

Availability varies by cloud and by whether you’re buying via a public listing or a private offer.

### Q: What is the difference between a public offer and a private offer?
- Public offer: Standard pricing/terms published in the marketplace.
- Private offer: A negotiated offer (price/commit/term) created for your account by Redwood and accepted through your marketplace procurement process.

If you require custom terms, committed spend, dedicated capacity reservations, or consolidated billing, a private offer is typically the right path.

### Q: Can my organization require marketplace procurement and still use the same Redwood product?
Yes. Marketplace procurement changes how subscription and billing are handled, but you use the same Redwood API/Console. Marketplace subscriptions are tied to entitlements that are linked to your Redwood organization.

### Q: Who should purchase (engineering vs procurement)?
Either is fine, but we recommend:
- Engineering initiates a subscription if you’re self-serve and ready to test quickly.
- Procurement initiates/approves a subscription if you need purchase controls, private offers, or contract review.

### Q: Do you support purchase orders (POs) via marketplace?
Marketplace purchases follow the marketplace billing model (charged through AWS/GCP). If you require a PO-driven process, many customers satisfy this via their cloud marketplace procurement setup. For questions specific to your AWS/GCP billing account configuration, your cloud provider account team can advise.

---

## 2) Getting started (subscription → access)

### Q: What are the onboarding steps after I subscribe?
Typical flow:
1) Subscribe to Redwood Inference in your marketplace (AWS or GCP)
2) Wait for entitlement propagation (usually minutes; sometimes longer)
3) Sign in (or create an account) in the Redwood Console
4) Link your marketplace subscription to a Redwood organization
5) Create an API key
6) Make your first API call

We provide step-by-step guides linked from the marketplace listing.

### Q: How long does it take for access to activate after subscribing?
Most activations complete within a few minutes. In some cases (cloud-side processing, account permissions, or entitlement propagation delays), it can take longer.

If you are blocked for more than 30–60 minutes after subscribing:
- Confirm you subscribed with the intended AWS/GCP billing account
- Confirm the user completing setup has permission to accept/activate marketplace subscriptions in your org
- Contact support@redwoodinference.com with your marketplace subscription identifier and your Redwood org name (if created)

### Q: I already have a Redwood organization. Can I link it to my marketplace subscription?
Yes. During onboarding, you can either:
- Link the subscription to an existing Redwood organization, or
- Create a new Redwood organization

If you have multiple teams, we recommend linking to the org that will own usage, API keys, and billing controls.

### Q: Can I have multiple marketplace subscriptions under the same Redwood org?
In many cases, yes (e.g., separate subscriptions for different products or environments). However, organizations should avoid overlapping subscriptions that could create confusion about entitlements and limits.

If you expect multiple subscriptions (e.g., separate business units or regions), contact Redwood to confirm the cleanest setup for quotas, billing visibility, and support routing.

### Q: What happens if I subscribe twice by accident?
No problem—this is a known edge case. Please contact support@redwoodinference.com with:
- The marketplace subscription IDs
- Your Redwood org name
- Which subscription should remain active

We’ll help you confirm entitlement linkage and avoid unexpected usage constraints.

---

## 3) Entitlements, limits, and usage

### Q: What is an “entitlement”?
An entitlement is the record that your marketplace subscription is active and what you’re entitled to use (e.g., which plan/SKU, included limits, and any committed terms). Redwood uses entitlements to provision access and enforce plan-specific constraints.

### Q: How are quotas/limits applied?
Quotas depend on the SKU you purchased (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and any add-ons). Once your subscription is linked, your Redwood org will reflect:
- Applicable rate limits / throughput limits
- Plan features and add-ons
- Any contract/commit-based constraints (where relevant)

Exact limits may vary by offer type and negotiated terms.

### Q: How do I verify my marketplace subscription is linked correctly?
In the Redwood Console, go to your organization’s billing/subscription area and confirm:
- Marketplace provider (AWS or GCP)
- Subscription status is Active
- Correct product/SKU is shown

If the Console shows “Pending” for an extended period, see the activation timing question above.

---

## 4) Billing, metering, and invoices

### Q: How will I be billed if I purchase via marketplace?
Marketplace purchases are billed through your cloud provider (AWS or GCP). Redwood reports metered usage (as applicable) to the marketplace, and the charges appear on your cloud bill under the Redwood marketplace product.

### Q: What usage is metered?
Metering depends on your SKU/offer. Common examples:
- Hosted API: usage-based (e.g., tokens processed, embeddings units), billed per the marketplace dimensions for the purchased SKU
- Dedicated capacity: reserved capacity dimension(s) or committed spend, depending on your offer structure
- Add-ons: may be billed as a recurring dimension (e.g., per month) or tied to usage, depending on the marketplace configuration

Your marketplace offer details define the billing dimensions and unit pricing.

### Q: Will Redwood also send me an invoice?
Typically, your invoice comes from AWS/GCP as part of your marketplace billing. Redwood can provide usage reporting and (for enterprise customers) billing reconciliation support, but the bill of record is the marketplace.

### Q: Where can I see detailed usage within Redwood?
In the Redwood Console you can view usage analytics (e.g., tokens, latency, errors) by model and route. This is operational usage visibility and may not exactly match how marketplace dimensions aggregate and round usage on your cloud invoice.

### Q: Why does my cloud invoice show different units/dimensions than the Redwood Console?
This can happen because:
- Marketplace dimensions can be aggregated differently (e.g., hourly/daily buckets)
- Rounding rules and reporting latency differ
- Some features are billed as add-ons or separate dimensions

If you suspect a mismatch, contact support@redwoodinference.com with:
- Cloud provider (AWS/GCP)
- Marketplace subscription ID
- The invoice line item / billing dimension name
- Time window in question

### Q: Do you support refunds/credits through marketplace?
Refunds and credits are governed by marketplace policies and your specific offer terms. If you believe you were billed incorrectly, contact Redwood support and we will work with you and the marketplace provider on next steps.

---

## 5) Trials, credits, and evaluation

### Q: Is there a free trial through AWS/GCP Marketplace?
Trial availability depends on the marketplace listing configuration and your organization’s procurement policies.

If a trial is not available via the marketplace listing, Redwood can often support evaluation via:
- A time-bound evaluation offer (often via private offer)
- A pilot plan with limited usage/capacity

Contact your account team or email sales@redwoodinference.com.

### Q: Can I use Redwood free credits if I’m buying via marketplace?
Marketplace billing is handled by AWS/GCP. In many cases, Redwood-issued product credits do not directly apply to marketplace invoices.

If you need an evaluation period, ask us about an evaluation offer structured for marketplace procurement.

---

## 6) Security, privacy, and compliance

### Q: Where can I find your marketplace security documentation?
We provide a marketplace-ready security packet that covers:
- Security overview and shared responsibility
- Data handling, retention, and residency options
- Encryption (in transit/at rest) and key management integrations
- Audit logging and export options
- Evidence pointers (SOC 2 / ISO-aligned controls)

Request links from your account team or see the links provided in the marketplace listing.

### Q: Is Redwood SOC 2 compliant?
Redwood maintains a SOC 2 program and can share relevant reports/evidence under appropriate access controls.

For procurement/security review, we can provide:
- SOC 2 report sharing workflow (under NDA / via a secure portal, as applicable)
- Control summaries and evidence pointers

### Q: How is my data encrypted?
Redwood supports encryption in transit (TLS) and encryption at rest for supported storage systems. For enterprise deployments, Redwood supports key management integrations (e.g., KMS/HSM options depending on deployment mode).

Specific details depend on whether you’re using Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment.

### Q: Do you store prompts and completions?
Data handling depends on product configuration and your purchased deployment mode.

At a high level:
- Redwood processes request content to generate responses and provide operational observability.
- Retention defaults and optional retention controls vary by product/deployment.

For exact retention behavior and configuration options, reference the marketplace data handling and retention documentation provided during security review.

### Q: Do you support audit logs?
Yes. Redwood provides audit logging for key account and security-relevant events (e.g., admin actions, API key management, org changes). Export options are available for enterprise workflows (e.g., SIEM ingestion).

Ask your account team for the “Audit logs for marketplace customers” overview.

### Q: Where is my data processed (data residency)?
Data processing regions depend on the deployment mode and the selected region(s). Some customers require specific region residency (e.g., US/EU). Redwood can support region-specific deployments and will document region commitments as part of enterprise onboarding.

If residency is a requirement, tell us:
- Required region(s)
- Whether you need single-region processing only
- Any restrictions on support access or cross-region failover

### Q: Can I use my own VPC / private networking?
Yes—Redwood offers Private deployment options (VPC and, in some cases, on-prem) designed for regulated workloads. Availability via marketplace depends on the listing/offer; many Private deployments are procured via private offer.

---

## 7) Support & escalation

### Q: How do I contact support if I purchased via marketplace?
Use the same support channels:
- Email: support@redwoodinference.com
- If you have an enterprise support plan, use your designated support channel and include your subscription details

Please include:
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace or GCP Marketplace
- Marketplace subscription ID (or offer ID if applicable)
- Your Redwood org name
- Error message / timestamp / request ID (if available)

### Q: What issues should I route to Redwood vs AWS/GCP?
Route to Redwood:
- Entitlement linking issues in the Redwood Console
- API errors, latency, model behavior, rate limiting questions
- Billing dimension questions and usage reconciliation
- Security documentation requests and questionnaires

Route to AWS/GCP (often with help from Redwood as needed):
- Cloud account permissions to subscribe/accept offers
- Marketplace procurement workflow questions
- Marketplace invoice payment processing

### Q: I subscribed but my org is still not provisioned. What should I do?
1) Confirm the subscription is Active in your marketplace console
2) Wait 10–15 minutes (entitlements may take time to propagate)
3) Retry linking in the Redwood Console
4) If still blocked after 30–60 minutes, contact Redwood support with your subscription ID

If this is production-blocking, mark the ticket as “Urgent” and include your impact description.

---

## 8) Common troubleshooting

### Q: The Console says “Entitlement not found.”
Most common causes:
- Entitlement propagation delay (try again in 10–15 minutes)
- You subscribed under a different cloud billing account than expected
- The user completing setup lacks permission to view/activate the marketplace subscription

If it persists, contact support with the subscription ID and cloud provider.

### Q: The Console says “Subscription already linked.”
This usually means the entitlement is already associated with a different Redwood org.

Contact support with:
- Subscription ID
- Intended Redwood org name
- Any existing org names you suspect it may be linked to

### Q: My invoice shows an unfamiliar billing dimension.
Send support:
- A screenshot or exact dimension name
- The time window
- Subscription ID

We’ll confirm the mapping and help reconcile with your purchased SKU.

---

## 9) Contact

- Support: support@redwoodinference.com
